description:
fix(docx): setting an indent clears the ISO-strict alias instead of conflicting

w:start / w:end are the ISO-strict spellings of w:left / w:right. A source that
uses them — Google Docs exports, Word for Mac — kept the OLD w:start next to the
NEW w:left we wrote, so the element ended up carrying two conflicting indents:

  before: 
  after:  

Word resolves that pair by its own preference, and any later normalizing save
collapses it by dropping one side — which is why the left indent appeared to
vanish on a subsequent round-trip while a re-issued set "fixed" it.

Clear the alias when writing the transitional attribute, mirroring the existing
firstLine/hanging pattern where setting one clears the other. Applied to both the
Set and Add paths (Add reuses an existing Indentation when the paragraph came
from a clone). Reading a source that only carries w:start is unchanged.

description:
fix(docx): style= given a display name says which channel resolves it

`style=`/`styleId=` target the OOXML styleId; `styleName=` is the channel that
resolves a display name through the styles part. Passing a display name to
`style=` — "heading 2" where the styleId is "Heading2", exactly the shape a Word
or Google Docs export has — stores a dangling pStyle that Word renders as body
text and drops on save. The advisory only said "not found in styles part", which
is true but a dead end: the style does exist, just under another id.

When the value matches an existing style's display name, the advisory now names
the resolving channel and the id it lands on:

  style 'heading 2' is a display name, not a styleId — will be referenced as-is.
  Use styleName='heading 2' to resolve it (styleId 'Heading2').

A value matching no style keeps the original wording, so nothing is mislabelled
as a display name. Applies to both the add and set paths.

Added

All event consume consumers share a single WSS connection managed by the bus daemon, which centralises handshake / heartbeat / auto-reconnect.
    • event list (cmd/event/list.go) — Lists subscribable EventKeys from the local built-in registry; does not require login and issues no remote calls. Optional --domain filters by domain (e.g. meeting); unknown domain exits with code 1 and prints the set of known domains.
    • event schema (cmd/event/schema.go) — Prints params_schema / resolved_output_schema / jq_root_path for the given EventKey; does not require login. Unknown key exits with code 1 pointing at event list. This is a mandatory pre-step before writing --jq / --param: a wrong jq_root_path does not error, it silently drops events (e.g. meeting.started / meeting.end have jq_root_path=.payload and payload itself is an array — jq must first do .[0] before descending into fields).
    • event consume --event-id (cmd/event/consume.go, cmd/event/consume_runner.go) — The actual subscription entry point; requires login (owner_hash is bound to the bus). Supports both batch mode (--max-events / --timeout) and long-running mode (neither flag, exit via Ctrl-C or event stop). Ships with --jq client-side projection, --param key=value for subscription parameters, --output-dir for NDJSON tee-to-disk (relative paths only, .. segments rejected — hard-validated), and --quiet to suppress non-fatal stderr. Strict stdout / stderr separation: business events go only to stdout NDJSON; ready markers / exit summaries / diagnostics go only to stderr. Once ready, stderr emits [event] ready event_key= (not muted by --quiet); on exit, stderr emits [event] exited — received event(s) in (reason: limit|timeout|signal|shutdown). Does not read stdin at all: closing stdin / < /dev/null / nohup / setsid will not trigger exit in either bounded or unbounded mode, making the command naturally compatible with agent / background scenarios. The stream does not replay historical events — only events newly produced after subscription are delivered.
    • event status (cmd/event/status.go, cmd/event/status_stop_test.go) — Inspects the local bus daemon state; does not require login and reads only the local bus directory. Lists buses[] with state: running / stale_owner (credential OpenId disagrees with bus owner) / orphan (pid dead but artefacts left behind) / refused / errored. Optional --fail-on-orphan exits with code 2 when an orphan is detected, useful for CI / self-healing scripts.
    • event stop (cmd/event/stop.go) — Stops the local bus daemon; does not require login. --force is treated as a write operation (enters the dangerous-operation confirmation table) and is used to reap orphan / stale_owner remnants; refused / errored states return exit code 2.
    • event _bus (cmd/event/bus.go) — Hidden subcommand forked automatically by event consume; agents must never invoke it directly. Owns the single WSS connection to the server, multiplexes subscribers, and fans events out to consumers over IPC (Unix socket / Windows named pipe).
    • Event framework internals (internal/event/bus, internal/event/source, internal/event/protocol, internal/event/protocol/wsspb, internal/event/busdiscover, internal/event/spawner, internal/event/transport, internal/event/cleanup, internal/event/jqfilter): Hub / subscription registry / connection management / WSS + protobuf codec (tmeet_wss.proto) / bus discovery + PID file / cross-platform detach fork (unix / windows) / cross-platform IPC transport / session keep-alive with token refresh / event de-duplication / jq projection engine with unit tests.
    • New exit-code contract: 0 (normal) / 1 (fatal: Hello rejected, unknown EventKey, IO error, subscription failure, ...) / 2 (only for event status --fail-on-orphan and event stop on refused / errored).
    • New SKILL section and reference doc (skills/tmeet-skill/references/tmeet-event.md, 483 lines): full coverage of use-case routing, mandatory call sequence, subprocess contract (ready / exited markers, exit codes, stdin EOF behaviour, stderr diagnostics), red lines (schema-before-jq, no kill -9, multi-account switching, path validation, privacy in output, _bus never called directly), bus-remnant self-heal flow, EventKey field reference, and a common-failure lookup table.

  • WSS endpoint constant (internal/core/endpoints.go): Endpoints.WSS and GetWSSEndpoint(), pointing to meeting.tencent.com, used by the event framework to open the WSS long connection.
  • config.ResourceReleaseHook teardown-hook mechanism (internal/config/user.go, internal/config/resource_hooks_test.go): New RegisterResourceReleaseHook / ResetResourceReleaseHooksForTest and a ClearUserConfigFunc type. Credential teardown (ClearUserConfig) now runs every registered hook first in registration order (fail-fast: any hook error or panic aborts teardown and leaves keychain + active_open_id intact so the user can retry), and only proceeds to keychain / meta cleanup if all hooks succeeded. cmd/root.go registers an event-bus hook via registerResourceReleaseHook() (dispatching to internal/event/cleanup.OnUserCleared) so auth logout and the refresh-token failure fallback gracefully stop the outgoing account's bus, preventing residue from leaking into the next login session. Deliberately placed in internal/config (the lowest package in the dependency graph) to avoid an internal/event → internal/config cycle.
  • Process-lifetime exclusive lock filelock.ProcessLock (internal/core/filelock/processlock.go, internal/core/filelock/filelock.go, internal/core/filelock/filelock_unix.go, internal/core/filelock/filelock_windows.go): Distinct from the existing short-lived WithLock (poll + defer auto-release), ProcessLock acquires non-blockingly and holds for the rest of the process; the OS releases it at process exit. Foundation for the bus daemon "am I alive?" probe (the bus takes a ProcessLock on bus.alive.lock at startup and never releases it; any subsequent TryLock succeeding means the previous holder died). The cross-platform lock primitives lockFDNonBlocking / unlockFD are extracted so both WithLock and ProcessLock share a single well-tested implementation.   • common.BuildUniqueID(openID, machineID) unifies Tmeet-Unique-ID / cli_uniq_id formatting (internal/common/system.go): The "*" concatenation is centralised in one helper. The REST proxy's Tmeet-Unique-ID request header and the WSS AuthBindReq.cli_uniq_id field now share the same implementation, ruling out format drift between the two paths.

  • Base64DecodeConverter no longer leaves RawStdEncoding / URLEncoding fields as raw ciphertext (internal/utils/converter.go): Previously the converter only fell back to RawURLEncoding once when StdEncoding decoding failed — coverage was incomplete: if the server returned RawStdEncoding (standard encoding without padding) or URLEncoding (URL-safe encoding with padding), decoding failed and the raw Base64 ciphertext was returned to the caller, surfacing as "an unreadable blob" in the model / user output. The converter now walks StdEncoding → RawStdEncoding → URLEncoding → RawURLEncoding in order, validating utf8.Valid on each success, and returns the decoded plaintext at the first hit; only if all four encodings fail does the original value pass through untouched.
  • CGI requests would fail wholesale when a stale proxy env var was inherited (internal/proxy/cgi-proxy/proxy.go, internal/core/thttp/client.go, internal/core/thttp/request.go): Agent-sandbox scenarios often set HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / ALL_PROXY pointing at a sidecar proxy, and a long-lived (or sandbox-spawned) tmeet process inherits those env vars.     • app set (cmd/app/set.go) — Updates the CLI app configuration via PUT /v1/cli/app-info. At least one of the three flags is required (MarkFlagsOneRequired); fields not provided are left untouched on the server side.
      • --homepage — App homepage URL. Non-empty: the CLI app is pushed to the meeting client and displayed in-meeting; empty string: the CLI app is no longer pushed in-meeting (this is effectively the "show in meeting" master switch). When non-empty, the URL is strictly validated by the new utils.ValidateURL (must start with http:// or https://, host non-empty) and length-capped to ≤ 200 characters via utils.CharacterLimit.
      • --layout-style — In-meeting open layout, validated client-side via the cmdutil.EnumValue type introduced in v1.0.15. Accepts only sidebar (narrow sidebar, 375px wide) / wide_sidebar (wide sidebar, 735px wide) / popout (standalone popout, 960×540px). When omitted, the CLI does not send the field: server default becomes sidebar if unset, existing value is preserved otherwise.
      • --sdk-name — In-meeting display name for the app. Length-capped at 20 in display width via the new utils.CharacterWidthLimit (ASCII counts as 1, non-ASCII such as Chinese counts as 2); also rejects pure-whitespace and empty strings.
  • New utils.ValidateURL URL validation helper (internal/utils/validate.go, internal/utils/validate_test.go): Built on net/url.Parse. Requires scheme to be http or https (case-insensitive), host to be non-empty, and rejects the empty string outright. Unit tests cover http/https, missing scheme, ftp://, empty host, and empty input. Currently consumed by app set's --homepage.
  • New utils.CharacterWidthLimit display-width limiter (internal/utils/string.go): Complements the v1.0.6 CharacterLimit (which counts UTF-8 runes) by counting display width — ASCII as 1, non-ASCII as 2. On overflow it returns an InvalidArgsError carrying the flag name, the configured limit, and the actual width. Currently consumed by app set's --sdk-name.
  • New ApiCmd constants (internal/cmdutil/api_schema.go): ApiCmdAppInfoSet / ApiCmdAppInfoGet — so the new app command group plugs into --compact and the middleware pipeline.

Changed

  • record list response now carries an extra state_int field (cmd/record/list.go): Before the raw state is transformed into a human-readable Chinese description by RecordStateConverter, the raw integer state code is recursively copied into a sibling state_int field via the new copyStateRaw / copyStateIntRecursive helpers. state_int is automatically appended to the --compact whitelist so it is preserved even in compact mode, letting callers programmatically branch on record state while keeping the human-readable description intact.
  • meeting get record enrichment now scopes recording queries by the meeting's time window (cmd/meeting/record_enrich.go): enrichMeetingWithFullRecords now reads each meeting object's start_time / end_time, parses them via parseUnixSeconds, and forwards them as start_time / end_time query params to the paginated recording-info API. This explicitly constrains the returned records to that meeting's time window and prevents cross-meeting historical records from bleeding into the enrichment.
  • SKILL bumped to 1.0.17 with the new app command group and related rules (skills/tmeet-skill/SKILL.md, skills/tmeet-skill/references/tmeet-app.md, skills/tmeet-skill/references/tmeet-meeting.md):
    • Top-level description extended: Adds "CLI 应用信息管理（设置/查询自己的 CLI 应用在会中的展示配置）" to the capability description.
    • Command tree extended with app group, linked to the new references/tmeet-app.md.
    • New references/tmeet-app.md reference doc: Fully covers the use-case table, get / set parameter tables, invocation rules (--homepage on/off semantics, URL legality, the http:// vs https:// protocol-selection decision table, https:// certificate-trust requirement, "--layout-style values must never be inferred"), and the post-success announcement rules (with heavy emphasis on the fact that set changes do not take effect in the currently-joined meeting — the user must rejoin to see the change, preventing agents from retrying set in a loop inside the same meeting).
    • http:// vs https:// client-compatibility decision table: Tencent Meeting client versions prior to 3.45.10 do not support opening http:// pages. For any http:// URL provided by the user, the agent must first confirm the client version before invoking app set, and must not skip the confirmation just because the user verbally claims to be on a "new version".
    • New error code 500294 handling rule (SKILL.md common-errors table + tmeet-app.md): When the current account's meeting plan does not entitle this feature, the backend returns an error description containing an upgrade link. The agent must return the URL verbatim and render it as a clickable Markdown link [升级会议套餐](URL) — no rewriting, no parameter dropping, no wrapping in backticks or code blocks, and no self-invented plan-type reasoning.
    • New error code 500284 handling rule (SKILL.md common-errors table): "该功能暂不可使用" — the current account has no entitlement (possibly ungrayed feature, insufficient commercial rights, etc.). Retries are strictly forbidden — the agent must inform the user truthfully that the feature is unavailable on the current account and that interpretation authority belongs to Tencent Meeting; it must not speculate on the cause or promise activation paths.
    • meeting update --meeting-type 1 usage clarified (references/tmeet-meeting.md): Corrects the over-strict wording from v1.0.16 ("modifying a recurring meeting requires --meeting-type 1"). The refined rule: --meeting-type 1 is required only when modifying recurrence rules (--recurring-type / --until-type / --until-count / --until-date) or modifying a specific sub-meeting (--sub-meeting-id). When only editing subject, time, password, join restrictions, watermark, recording, or invitees — i.e. non-recurrence fields — --meeting-type is not required; the server will not silently downgrade a recurring meeting to a regular one, and the recurrence rule is preserved.
  • README sync (README.md / README_EN.md): Command tree extended with app get / app set; new app section with parameter table and examples (client 3.45.10 compatibility notice, https:// certificate-trust requirement, --sdk-name display-width cap, and the three --layout-style options).

Fixed

  • meeting create / meeting update gating logic for --join-type and --waiting-room corrected (cmd/meeting/create.go, cmd/meeting/update.go): Previously --join-type was gated by > 0 and --waiting-room was gated by the bool value, which caused two bugs: (1) explicitly passing --join-type 0 was silently dropped and never sent to the server; (2) update could not turn waiting-room off once it had been turned on — the bool zero value false was indistinguishable from "flag not provided" and was skipped. Both flags now use cmd.Flags().Changed(...) — consistent with other advanced-setting fields (--water-mark-type, etc.): if the user did not explicitly pass the flag, nothing is sent and the server value is preserved; only explicit input is written into settings. Users can now reliably switch join-type back to "all members" and turn off an already-enabled waiting room.

feat(email-core): guard against caller-replayed duplicate delivery (#209)

* feat(email-core): guard against caller-replayed duplicate delivery

`isRetryable(err, 'delivery') === false` and the single-attempt dispatch in
send_email/reply_to_email/send_draft guarantee that this library never
re-issues a send. They guarantee nothing about the caller, and the caller is
the one that replays.

The residual hole: an agent whose tool result was lost — a compacted context, a
dropped transport, a supervisor restarting the turn, a person retrying a call
that looked stuck — re-issues the identical instruction, and the second call is
indistinguishable from a first one. The only defence was a sentence of English
in each tool description ("do not resend without checking Sent Items"), which
is exactly the guard an LLM under retry pressure skips. When it fails it fails
silently: the second send succeeds and the recipient gets the message twice.

Provider endpoints take no idempotency key, so this cannot be fixed at the
provider boundary. It is fixed one level up, with the state nothing previously
held: an in-process ledger keyed by a digest of what would actually be
delivered — mailbox, recipients, subject, rendered post-truncation body,
attachment content hashes, scheduled time, and the reply parent or draft id.
The record is written BEFORE dispatch, so the reserved window is exactly the
window in which an acknowledgement gets lost, and settled after.

Three refusal codes rather than one, because the recovery differs:
DUPLICATE_SEND_IN_FLIGHT (wait), DUPLICATE_SEND_BLOCKED (stop — the prior
messageId comes back with it), DUPLICATE_SEND_UNRESOLVED (a human checks Sent
Items).

Release is an allowlist, not a denylist. Only codes that PROVE non-delivery —
4xx-derived, 429, connect-failure — free the fingerprint, so a resend after a
rejection is never blocked. Everything else, including a code no provider has
shown us yet, is held. A wrongly-held message costs one refused resend and
prints the override; a wrongly-released one costs a duplicate in somebody's
inbox, which is the bug being fixed.

On by default, with no embedder wiring. ActionContext.sendLedger exists only so
tests can inject an isolated ledger; when absent the actions fall back to the
process default. ActionContext.rateLimiter is the cautionary example — an
optional injected interface that no shipped adapter constructs, so the rate
limit it documents does not exist in the product. A guard someone has to
remember to wire is a guard that is off.

send_draft claims before the draft lookup, not after: a provider that consumed
the draft on the first send makes the second lookup fail, and "cannot verify
draft recipients" is a misleading answer to "did this already go out?". Every
bail-out between claim and dispatch releases.

allow_duplicate: true is the deliberate escape hatch, and re-arms the guard
against its own replay.

Limitation, stated rather than papered over: the ledger is per-process and in
memory. It closes the replay window that actually occurs — a retry inside a
running server — and does not survive restarting that server. Cross-process
durability needs a persisted store and is deliberately not attempted here.

Evidence: 559 email-core tests pass (up from 546). Negative control run —
rebuilding the suite with the ledger window forced to 0 turns 6 of the new
assertions red and leaves the three that assert non-blocking behavior green, so
the tests can fail. A separate check drives the built dist through an
ActionContext with no sendLedger and confirms the unwired production path is
guarded; it is kept as the "Guard is active without embedder wiring" test
rather than as a one-off script.

Ref: openspec/changes/add-duplicate-send-guard

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HkdNf9x4QS4LYS2DSiQWXS

* fix(email-core): bind ledger settlement to the attempt that produced it

Codex peer review found five executable defects in the duplicate-send guard.
Each was reproduced against the tree before being fixed, and each now has a
regression test that fails without the fix.

1. Settle and release addressed only the fingerprint, so they acted on whatever
   attempt occupied the key. A fingerprint can legitimately carry two live
   attempts, because allow_duplicate creates one. Interleaving: A dispatches; a
   forced B dispatches and succeeds; A comes back rejected and DELETES B's
   successful record; an ordinary replay then sends a third copy. Attempts now
   carry an identity and the claim closure holds its own entry.

2. A forced claim discarded the prior record before the forced send was known
   to have delivered, so a rejected override erased the delivery it was
   overriding and the next ordinary call sent again. No concurrency needed. The
   forced attempt is now recorded alongside the earlier one. Same defect at the
   action layer in send_draft: forcing a consumed draft failed its lookup,
   released, and left an ordinary replay reporting DRAFT_LOOKUP_FAILED instead
   of naming the message that had already gone out.

3. The process-default ledger was keyed on ctx.mailboxName, which is optional.
   Two mailboxes in one process shared the empty key: the second mailbox's
   FIRST EVER send was refused and handed the first mailbox's message id — a
   wrong refusal and a cross-mailbox identifier leak in one response. The
   namespace now falls back to a per-provider-instance id held in a WeakMap.
   The shipped MCP wrapper always supplies a resolved name, so this was the
   library and default-context surface, not that server.

4. A success that settled after its reservation had been pruned was dropped on
   the floor, admitting an immediate replay of a message that had just been
   delivered. A late settlement is re-inserted and dated from settlement.

5. Size-cap eviction could evict an in-flight reservation — dropping cover for
   a send that is on the wire, the worst thing this module can do. Eviction now
   takes the oldest SETTLED attempt and never an active one. A burst of
   concurrent sends may briefly carry the map past the cap; refusing a claim
   because the ledger is full would block first-ever sends, which is worse.

Also from the review, verified at each production site:

- DELIVERY_PROVEN_UNSENT_CODES was incomplete for the shipped providers. Graph
  REPLY_FAILED (prepareReplyDraft throws before /send),
  ATTACHMENT_TOO_LARGE_FOR_PROVIDER (size validation, zero POSTs),
  ATTACHMENT_UPLOAD_FAILED (draft created, /send never called) and
  SCHEDULE_DRAFT_FAILED (no draft id, no deferred-send time) all provably
  deliver nothing, yet each held a fingerprint and produced a false refusal.
- Gmail reported a delivery whose connection never opened as generic
  PROVIDER_ERROR, which cannot be released because the same code also covers
  failures that are not proven. It now reports PROVIDER_UNREACHABLE for that
  transport condition, matching what the Graph provider already does. Generic
  PROVIDER_ERROR is deliberately NOT added to the allowlist.

Documentation corrections, including one claim that was false when written:

- The proposal said the ledger stores a "salted digest". No salt was ever
  implemented. Corrected in place with a note saying what it previously
  claimed, rather than quietly deleted.
- The spec said a colliding claim SHALL NOT "invoke the provider". Too broad:
  reply_to_email reads the parent message before consulting the ledger, and
  send_draft reads the draft. It is the delivery dispatch that is suppressed.
- The override was described as replacing the prior record. It is recorded
  alongside it, and allow_duplicate is an unconditional per-request bypass — a
  replay that itself carries the flag dispatches again. Nothing here makes the
  forced request idempotent.
- The README described the fingerprint as the bytes that leave the process.
  Providers transform outbound mail (Graph truncates a subject at 255), so it
  is the effective action inputs. The guard catches a replayed tool call.

Evidence: 569 email-core tests and 119 provider-gmail tests pass, up from 559
and 116. Codex's own 13 executable probes go from 1 passing to 11; the two that
remain are the ones it classified as out of scope for this commit — the
pre-existing scheduled-send fallback code, fixed separately next, and the
provider-truncation equivalence, which is addressed as wording above.

Ref: openspec/changes/add-duplicate-send-guard
Ref: .peer-review/dup-send-guard-1788823130-24309-codex.md

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HkdNf9x4QS4LYS2DSiQWXS

* fix(email-core): report an unclassified scheduling throw as ambiguous

Scheduling is a two-write draft→send. When the provider itself classifies a
failure the action passes that code through, but the catch-all fallback for an
unclassified throw was SCHEDULE_SEND_FAILED — a terminal code asserting the
submission was rejected, for an outcome that proves nothing of the kind.

handleProviderError already states the rule in its own doc comment: for a
delivery operation the fallback MUST be an ambiguous code, because an
unclassified failure on a send is exactly the case where we cannot prove the
message did not go out. The immediate-send path follows it; the scheduled path
did not. A caller told "failed" for a submission that may have been queued is
being invited to schedule a duplicate.

The fallback becomes SCHEDULE_SEND_STATUS_UNKNOWN, and quota is charged on it
for the same reason the non-throw branch two lines above already charges it.
SCHEDULE_SEND_FAILED is unchanged where the Microsoft provider classifies a 4xx
rejection — that code is still correct and still proves non-delivery.

Found during Codex peer review of the duplicate-send guard and confirmed to
predate it, so it lands as its own commit rather than inside that change. The
guard was already correct here regardless: an unclassified throw settles with
no code and is held as unresolved, so a replay was refused either way. This
fixes what the CALLER is told.

Tests: the ambiguous fallback, plus a negative control asserting a
provider-classified SCHEDULE_SEND_FAILED still surfaces as terminal — without
it the fix could have blurred the distinction it exists to preserve.

feat: support developer sandboxes, free, and paid teams as install targets (#147)

* feat: offer ranked install targets beyond developer sandboxes

The Slack CLI logs into any workspace the developer belongs to, but
`create-slack-app` treated a developer sandbox as the only option, which
put Developer Program signup on the critical path for anyone trying the
plugin for the first time.

Step 3 is now "Choose Where to Install the App" and presents three
ranked targets: a developer sandbox (recommended), a Free Team (second
choice), or an existing production workspace (last resort). Each gets
its own sub-step with the constraint that actually bites: sandboxes need
a Developer Program account, Free Teams cap at 10 apps, and production
workspaces are usually gated by admin app approval, which is always on
for Enterprise Grid and switchable on elsewhere.

`test-slack-app` no longer implies a sandbox is the only safe place to
test. The warning it was carrying is right about a workspace with real
coworkers in it and wrong about a throwaway Free Team, so it now asks
which of the three the developer is pointed at rather than asking them
to confirm a sandbox.

Two smaller corrections while in here:

- `sandbox create` is not interactive when given `--name` and
  `--password`; the prompts are fallbacks for missing flags. The skill
  can run it directly instead of handing it to the developer. `sandbox
  list` needs `--team` for the same reason.
- Nothing this skill scaffolds can trip `free_team_not_allowed`, which
  is scoped to low-code workflow and function apps. Bolt apps install
  and run on the free plan.

* chore: reword the changeset to name all three install targets

Matches the PR title. The changeset summary ships in the CHANGELOG, so
it carries the same framing as the title rather than the earlier
"ranked install targets" phrasing.

* chore: trim the target list out of the create-slack-app description

The three targets are Step 3's content, and naming them in the
description bought nothing that Step 3 does not already do. Trigger cues
